item.title: Cody Campbell once again makes it about himself
item.description: Credit: Keith Inglis on X If there’s anybody who perfectly encapsulates the “get in there and make it about you” meme, it’s Texas Tech booster and oil tycoon Cody Campbell. Campbell has taken on outsized influence in not just investing millions in the Red Raiders athletic program to bring their teams to prominence, but throughout all of college football as well. He has been vocal in advocating for sweeping, transformational changes to the sport, particularly around the Protect College Sports Act and nationalizing television rights . But he has also rubbed others the wrong way with how he handles his business. He publicly clashed with former Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark with complaints over Friday night scheduling. And he’s shown himself to be a bit overly sensitive as he threatened a Lubbock radio station with pulling players from interviews over a critical tweet from a producer. He also regularly positions himself as part of the program through his appearances and messaging, acting as more of an owner or general manager than booster. So when Texas Tech clinched a Big 12 championship game appearance with a victory over TCU on Friday night, it was no surprise that Cody Campbell found a way to elbow himself into the spotlight. The booster showed up at the postgame press conference to ask a question to head coach Joey McGuire about the team having the momentum of a runaway freight train and why he’s so popular. Full exchange between Texas Tech mega-booster Cody Campbell and head coach Joey McGuire as he sat in on the postgame press conference following a win over TCU. Campbell’s question: “So, with all the adversity we dealt with over the last year, everything we’ve been through, can you talk about and I because I’ve seen it, the love that you have for your players, the love they have for you and and for each other, and how that’s gotten us through everything we’ve dealt with and why we’re in the place we’re in once again this year?” — Keith Inglis (@KeithInglisDT) November 27, 2026 Naturally, Cody Campbell will say that he’s only doing this because he wants McGuire and the team to get the respect and love that they are due and it’s all about lifting them up. But in reality, he’s only taking the attention for himself once again. There is no reason for him to be showing up and asking questions at a postgame press conference. None. But because he is the one that’s paying for all of this, he can do whatever he wants. If Campbell really wanted McGuire and the team to get some shine, the best thing he could do is get out of the way and let them actually have the moment for themselves. But that’s something that he seems incapable of understanding. The post Cody Campbell steals the spotlight in crashing Texas Tech press conference appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Jackson Koivun Wins The 2026 Skins Game
item.description: HOBE SOUND, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 27: Jackson Koivun of the United States plays his shot from the seventh tee during the Farmers Insurance Skins Game at Atlantic Fields Club on November 27, 2026 in Hobe Sound, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) Getty Images Last year saw the return of the popular golf event call the Skins Game. What used to be a staple for golf fans during the offseason stopped abruptly in 2008 returned in 2025 for Black Friday viewing. This event brings together four PGA Tour pros to compete in a friendly but high-stakes competition with a total purse of $4 million dollars. The 2026 event had the following golfers competing for big-time money. 2026 Skins Game Participants: Justin Thomas Wyndham Clark Brooks Koepka Jackson Koivun The event, which took place at The Atlantic Fields Club in Hobe Sound, Florida, returned to its original format of the event. The competition, which started back in 1983, abandoned the “reverse purse” from 2025, in which each player started with $1 million and the amount went up or down based on whether a player won or lost a hole. For many viewers and spectators, it didn’t resound as much as the older format. The old format, for those who don’t remember, has each player starting at $0, making every hole’s value clearer and more obvious. Each hole carries a dollar value and tied holes will roll over, which can raise the stakes rather quickly. All golfers involved in this year’s event are first-time players in the Skins Game, but it was Justin Thomas who was slated to be in last year’s event before undergoing offseason back surgery and having to remove himself from the field. Unlike 2025, where Xander Schauffele failed to win even a single skin during the event, this event was competitive till the very end. This year there was a serious carryover down the stretch which resulted in an 18th hold worth $2 million dollars. No one could win the hole out-right, which meant they headed to a “19th” hole. The tee box was placed 118 yards from the pin on the 18th hole, and every player got a shot. Closest to the hole, while hitting the green, won the $2 million dollars. Thomas was up first, and missed the green long. Second was Clark, and he too missed the green, landing on the fringe. Koepka was third to hit, and he hit a safe shot in the middle of the green. The pressure was on the 21-year-old Koivun to put his shot inside Koepka, and the result was extremely close to Koepka. The result required an official measurement, which showed Koivun won the hole, and the event. The shot equated in Koivun winning $2.375-million, a total which topped his career earnings so far on the PGA Tour. When all was said and done, the money totals were as follows for the event: Jackson Koivun: $2.375 Million Brooks Koepka: $700,000 Justin Thomas: $475,000 Wyndham Clark: $400,000 The event was much more competitive than the 2025 iteration, and should be deemed as a success. item.title: Opinion: Why Doesn’t Arteta Play His Strikers Together More Often?
item.description: Opinion: Why Doesn’t Arteta Play His Strikers Together More Often? I am not a football manager or a football expert, and I don’t try to be, but I like to think I know a bit about football, having played the game myself for a number of years alongside being a huge football fan, watching many leagues and teams over the years, but most of all, of course, being a passionate Arsenal fan. Now, this may be controversial, but everyone is allowed an opinion, and I like to think, well, I hope, I know what I’m talking about sometimes. But what I would like to see is Mikel Arteta take the risk and sometimes play with two strikers up front. The rest of the formation and the way he decides to set up his team would not be a problem, but I’d genuinely like to see two up front. Why Not Play Havertz and Gyökeres Together? Now, I say this because, as we know, he seems to pick between either Kai Havertz or Viktor Gyökeres, and he rarely goes for the two of them together. But why not? If you haven’t tried it regularly, how do you know if it will work? Now, I don’t mean try it once and if it doesn’t work, give up. I mean give the two a chance to play together on a number of occasions! Everyone has their moans and groans when our strikers are not scoring, and yes, sometimes the delivery is not what it should be, but sometimes you have to take the game into your own hands and try, as we saw with Gyökeres’ goal against Borussia Dortmund the other night, which was a rather sweet strike. So why does Gyökeres seem to score left, right and centre for Sweden but struggle for Arsenal? There may be a number of reasons, but one reason I believe is because he is high in confidence, and more often than not, he is not playing as a lone striker as he tends to do for Arsenal. Sweden seems to have built their team around Gyökeres, and in the Nations League this year he has often played in a strike partnership, notably alongside Liverpool’s Alexander Isak, hence the great goalscoring form for his country. He scored six goals in five Nations League games this campaign and recently made history by scoring in eight consecutive matches in the competition , across two editions, scoring 12 goals during that run. Gyökeres is a player who can hold the ball up well and make that pass, whereas Havertz tends to struggle in that department depending on who is defending him. But he can offer good off-the-ball movement and good link-up play to the team. So why can the two not play together? (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images) Could a Strike Partnership Bring More Goals? Gyökeres reminds me a bit of Olivier Giroud at times with the hold-up play and the running off the shoulder, but we know back in Giroud’s Arsenal playing days he had support from other strikers most of the time when he wasn’t deployed as a focal striker. item.title: Section 1 moving forward with plan to separate non-public schools during playoffs, despite state objections
item.description: Section 1 is moving forward with a plan that would separate its public and non-public schools during postseason athletic competition, despite the move previously being overturned by a NYSPHSAA appeals panel. (Jim Franco/Times Union) When the Christian Brothers Academy football team takes the field Saturday night at Middletown High School for a Class AA state semifinal against Section 1's Mamaroneck, the Brothers will be doing so against a team from a section that is attempting to separate its public and non-public schools during postseason competition. A win Saturday in Middletown could also put CBA on a collision course for a state championship matchup next week against Syracuse's Christian Brothers Academy. If both CBA teams win their state semifinals this weekend, it would mark the second time in three years that the state title in New York's largest classification is contested between the two private schools that share the same name. First up for the Albany CBA squad is its matchup against Mamaroneck on Saturday at 6 p.m. The Tigers represent Section 1, which recently announced that despite objections from the New York State Public High School Athletic Association, it was moving forward with a planned change to its constitution that would separate private, parochial and charter schools from public schools during postseason athletic competition. That move would leave the non-public schools ineligible to participate in state playoffs. Section 1 announced the change to its constitution in June, following a 69-4 vote of member schools in the section, which includes Westchester, Rockland, Putnam and Dutchess counties. Section 1's four non-public members - Albertus Magnus in Nanuet, Ursuline School in New Rochelle, Keio Academy in Purchase and The Lefell School in Hartsdale - were the only four institutions in the section to vote against the amendment. Three of the affected non-public schools filed an appeal with NYSPHSAA, and in July a three-person appeals panel from the state association ruled to overturn that amendment. However, at its October meeting, Section 1 announced plans to move forward with its plan beginning in the 2027-28 school year. In a statement to the Times Union, a Section 1 spokesperson said: "In June, 69 of the 73 schools that cast ballots supported proceeding with the changes, exceeding the two-thirds approval required for passage. Section One's decision to move forward with amendments to its constitution and bylaws is a matter of internal governance and reflects the direction of its member schools." The issue of private, parochial and charter schools - dubbed "schools without boundaries" by NYSPHSAA - competing against public institutions in state championship events has been a hot-button topic in recent years. NYSPHSAA convened an ad hoc committee to address the issue in 2024, which ultimately adopted a plan to provide statewide standards for reclassifying non-public and charter schools based on performance. item.title: Alaves star heaps praise on Jude Bellingham ahead of Real Madrid clash: ‘He’s a great player’
item.description: Alaves star heaps praise on Jude Bellingham ahead of Real Madrid clash: ‘He’s a great player’ Real Madrid will look to extend their winning run to 11 games in all competitions as they take on Deportivo Alaves this weekend. Heading into the clash, Alaves midfielder Antonio Blanco addressed the media as he offered his thoughts on facing Real Madrid and what it means to him as a player. Blanco came through the ranks at Real Madrid, even making his first-team debut, with Los Blancos still holding 50% of his transfer rights as part of his €4 million move to Alaves in 2023. Blanco wary of Bellingham threat First and foremost, Blanco was asked about the prospect of facing an in-form Jude Bellingham, who has found his best form under the leadership of Jose Mourinho. Blanco has immense respect for Jude Bellingham. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “We know he’s a great player, but we’ll try to stop him. Madrid have many top-level footballers. We have to focus on doing our job to get a good result,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). Blanco, who has rediscovered his best form after a difficult patch, is relishing a packed schedule that sees Alaves play three games in seven days across LaLiga and the Copa del Rey. “What we like is to play matches and if it’s for three days, then all the better. You’re constantly with the tension of competition. Besides, the Copa del Rey is also coming up, a very nice competition that we enjoy playing,” he explained. Confidence heading to the Bernabeu Deportivo Alaves will have a tough challenge on their hands. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Deportivo Alaves will face an intense challenge against an in-form Real Madrid squad. But Blanco believes his team can cause an upset. “We go with confidence after breaking a run where we were struggling. The other day against Deportivo we got the three points and recovered our DNA. We’ll see how tomorrow’s game goes,” he said. Finally, Blanco played down the significance of Alaves’ narrow 2-1 defeat at the Bernabeu back in April. “Better not to look for references. We know they’re in great form. In the top flight any team can complicate your life. You have to give one hundred percent from everyone to try to bring back the three points,” he concluded.

item.title: In-form O'Leary out to defy old club Bristol City
item.description: Reunion day at The Hawthorns as Max O'Leary and Jed Wallace both prepare to face their former clubs [Shutterstock] West Bromwich Albion goalkeeper Max O'Leary has been in the form of his life this season, rescuing the Baggies on numerous occasions with some outstanding saves to keep them right in the heat of Championship promotion contention. But it is one save he actually failed to make that has dominated the build-up to Saturday's meeting with his boyhood club Bristol City at The Hawthorns. Bath-born O'Leary actually made his professional debut at The Hawthorns in a 2-2 FA Cup third-round tie between Albion and City back in January 2016 as a half-time substitute for injured visiting keeper Frank Fielding. And, when Albion scrambled in a 95th-minute equaliser to earn an Ashton Gate replay, which the Baggies went on to win, the scorer who left him on his knees in despair was none other than home midfielder James Morrison, now the Albion boss. "Yes, he managed to score against me in my first-ever game," O'Leary this week told BBC Radio Bristol's Sound of the City. "And he's mentioned it a few times since." Morrison confident Price will 'heal quickly' After 13 years on the books at Ashton Gate, during which he made 179 City appearances and had loan spells at Kidderminster Harriers, Bath City, Solihull Moors and Shrewsbury Town, he finally left 11 months ago to join Albion. And, ahead of his first meeting with City since, which also involves former Baggies skipper Jed Wallace potentially lining up against his old club, it has all gone rather nicely for O'Leary. "A lot of footballers just want to know where they stand," he added. "Ultimately i got that answer and moved on to a new challenge, which was the best thing for me - and it's worked out well so far." James Morrison regularly reminds his Baggies keeper Max O'Leary of the injury-time equaliser he scored for Albion to earn a 2-2 FA Cup draw with Bristol City in 2016 [Shutterstock] After proving a key part of Albion's improved late-season rescue following Morrison's installation as boss, O'Leary's tally of only 18 league goals conceded in 17 games this season is the third-best in the Championship, bettered only by Birmingham City and Southampton. That included a key save in Wednesday night's 3-1 win at Bolton, which kept the Baggies 13 points ahead of the 16th-placed Robins. "He didn't have a lot to do in the first half," said Morrison. "But, when he's called upon, he's producing it, which is the sign of a good goalkeeper who's confident and enjoying his football. "That save probably won us the game. And he now just has to keep doing that. He's got nothing to prove, facing his old club. He's been a tremendous addition." item.title: Jamie Overton's maiden five-for powers England to seven-wicket win over Australia, take 2-1 series lead
item.description: England produced a dominant all-round performance to defeat Australia by seven wickets (DLS method) in a rain-affected third T20I at the Gabba in Brisbane on Friday. Jamie Overton starred with a maiden five-wicket haul in international cricket as the visitors chased down the revised target to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series. Having won the toss and elected to bowl, England made full use of the conditions to bundle out Australia for just 108 in 16.5 overs. Overton returned remarkable figures of 5/12, while Liam Dawson picked up three wickets for 16 runs to dismantle the Australian batting line-up. The victory also marked Australia's lowest-ever men's T20I total on home soil, adding to an unforgettable outing for England's bowling attack. Jamie Overton's maiden five-wicket haul dismantles Australia Australia struggled to build momentum after being asked to bat first, with England striking at regular intervals. Liam Dawson provided the early breakthrough by dismissing Mitchell Marsh for 11, while Overton took catches at mid-on to remove the Australian captain and Sam Harper, who scored 26 off 14 deliveries. Jake Fraser-McGurk attempted to provide some momentum with an aggressive 22 off 11 balls but was deceived by Overton's extra bounce in the seventh over. The England all-rounder then took complete control of the innings, picking up wickets in each of his next two overs. He dismissed Nikhil Chaudhary for 19 before removing Ben Dwarshuis for a duck to complete his maiden five-wicket haul in international cricket. Overton finished with outstanding figures of 5/12, including 17 dot balls, while Dawson claimed 3/16. The duo ensured Australia were reduced to 92/7 before the lower order was eventually wrapped up. Mitchell Owen offered some resistance with 17 runs, but his attempt to drag Australia towards a competitive total ended with a run-out in the 17th over. Sam Curran then bowled Billy Stanlake, leaving the hosts all out for 108 in 16.5 overs. Australia's 108-run total became their lowest-ever score in a men's T20I on home soil, surpassing their previous lowest of 111 against New Zealand in Sydney in 2022. It was also Australia's second-lowest T20I total against England, behind their 79 all out at Southampton in 2005. Additionally, the score marked the lowest first-innings total recorded at the Gabba in T20 cricket. Australia pacer Riley Meredith provided some resistance by removing Phil Salt for five before dismissing Aneurin Donald, who had given England a flying start with an aggressive 32 off 13 deliveries. item.title: Sporting JAX defender earns second Scotland national team selection
item.description: Sporting Club Jacksonville Sporting Club Jacksonville defender Georgia Brown has earned a selection to the Scotland Women’s National Team for the upcoming FIFA Women’s World Cup second-round play-off matches against Sweden. The roster spot marks the second international call-up of the season for the 24-year-old defender, who competes professionally in the Gainbridge Super League. A victory over Sweden across the two-legged aggregate series would secure Scotland a place in the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. Qualification would mark only the second time in the national team’s history that it has reached the tournament. Brown was previously selected for Scotland’s qualifying matches against Czechia in October. Brown has started 11 Gainbridge Super League matches on the back line for Sporting JAX this season. She noted that representing her country offers a meaningful opportunity to compete for a World Cup spot. “It’s an incredible honor to represent Scotland; I’m extremely grateful every time I get to put the shirt on and the feeling of playing for something so much bigger than yourself is incredible,” Brown said. “And especially with the opportunity to qualify for the World Cup, that’s something every footballer dreams of, so it’s a really exciting time.” Brown explained that participating in national team camps contributes to her overall development on the pitch. She pointed to the daily standard of training with experienced teammates as an asset that sharpens her understanding before returning to club competition on the First Coast. “I feel like I gain something each time I go away with the squad,” Brown said. “The attention to detail and intensity of the sessions and games at camp helps raise my own level and improves my understanding of the game, which I try to show when I get back to Jacksonville. Just being surrounded by players who have lots of experience playing at the highest level allows me to learn so much about how they prepare for and approach games, especially during high-pressure moments.” Following the selection, JAX congratulated Brown on her call-up and wished her luck with the national team. Scotland will host Sweden for the first leg on Tuesday, Dec. 1. item.title: Italy edge out Fiji in Nations Championship at sparse Twickenham
item.description: Italy take on Fiji as the sides battle to avoid bottom spot – not that it could tempt many to attend the match - PA/Mike Egerton Italy ended their seven-match losing streak to edge Fiji 23-21, but the clash between the Nations Championship’s lowest ranked teams was watched by a sparse crowd at Allianz Stadium. Billed as the “Super Bowl of rugby”, finals weekend has struggled to attract interest with only 32,000 general admission tickets sold for day one, resulting in Twickenham’s top tier being closed. Acting as the curtain raiser to the fifth place play-off between Ireland and Australia later on Friday night, Fiji and Italy at least delivered a hard-fought battle that went down to the wire. Sumptuous second-half tries by Peniasi Dakuwaqa and Kitione Salawa propelled the Islanders into the lead, reeling in Italy who had established a 17-0 lead built on touch downs by Federico Mori and Giacomo Nicotera. Ultimately it was the boot of Tommaso Allan that proved the difference with the former Harlequins full-back landing a decisive 68th minute penalty to complete a 13-point individual haul. Fiji played some thrilling rugby in pursuit of a late victory but their execution was poor with a knock-on close to the line and wayward line-out throw important moments that cost them. Italy defended well and showed greater discipline to end a losing run that dated back to their historic victory over England in the penultimate round of the Six Nations. 06:45pm This weekend’s fixtures Today: Fiji 21 Italy 23 Ireland vs Australia 8.10pm Saturday: Wales vs Japan 1.10pm England vs New Zealand 4.40pm Sunday: Scotland vs Argentina 1.10pm South Africa vs France 4.40pm 06:43pm Man of the match Ross Vintcent “It was physical, full credit to Fiji. item.title: Xavier 71 – 83 Virginia: Just please make a shot
item.description: I’m assuming he’s pondering all those misses | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was hard to determine what was more infuriating today: the announcers, the officials, or Xavier’s steadfast refusal to make shots that matter. Virginia is an extremely good team, but Xavier made it a bit too easy for them today. For a game that tipped off absurdly early, this one turned into a decent contest once it got rolling. That took some time though, and by the time X had warmed to it, the Cavaliers had done what they needed to win. If you don’t believe me, ask the announcing crew that seemed to be Virginia grads (or possibly Chance Mallory’s uncles). With 12:12 to go in the first half, Mike Nwoko (15/4/1) was called for his second foul. I say called for, not committed, because it was a bad call. It functionally changed the game. Nwoko was too much for Virginia to handle when he was in, but he would get only 40 more seconds in the first half. Xavier ended that first half in a 15 point hole. Nwoko likely wouldn’t have scored 15 in the first half, but he would have made a difference. For the game his +/- was zero. X didn’t get the chance to find out if that would have held, because he had to watch. But Xavier also didn’t help themselves. They were hideous from the floor (39.3%), from behind the arc (1-8), and from the line (4-8) in the first half. That is appalling shooting and has been the story of the season so far. For the game the team was hardly any better, shooting .393/.227/.621. You can complain about the refereeing, which I found to be quite uneven, but you won’t win any games being that pitiful from deep or the line. Xavier is 332nd in the nation from the line. Had they made just four more, this game would have been different. That would have been 75%. Had they made two more three pointers, still a pitiful 32%, you could add six more points. That’s an easy, easy , ten points that Xavier left on the floor. Toss in 9-22 on layups and, well, you get it. Which is a shame, because they defended well enough to win. The Musketeers forced 21 turnovers and pressured the Cavaliers into missing six layups. Virginia ended up scoring 1.1 points per possession, but that came largely on good shooting from deep (12-30) and is still hardly an insurmountable number. It is insurmountable, though, if you leave easy points on the floor all game. Xavier’s defensive pressure was fun to watch, but when they couldn’t get out and run or at least create in transition, they couldn’t score. Ruben Dominguez is adding nothing to this team Dominguez is here for games like this. His whole raison d’etre is making three pointers. He hasn’t done that this season and he didn’t again today. He played nine minutes here today and played his second game where he made so little impact that he didn’t merit an offensive rating. Add in a 13 minute 0 offensive efficiency against Iowa and you have three games in which he has been so bad he’s been nothing. That means in 31 minutes over three games

The 22-year-old has become one of the Premier League’s standout young full-backs and, crucially, Newcastle’s stance is emphatic. Hall is viewed as “strictly not for sale”, and it would reportedly take a fee “north of £66million” to even open discussions. That figure would move beyond the current world-record level for a left-back, which tells its own story about how highly he is valued at St James’ Park. Hall only signed a new long-term contract in September, tying him to Newcastle until 2031. That commitment has not quietened outside interest. That does not mean a deal is imminent, far from it, though it does indicate serious appreciation from Anfield decision-makers. The reasoning is clear enough. TeamTalk states Liverpool’s recruitment staff have concerns over “the lack of progress shown by Milos Kerkez” since his £40m move from Bournemouth in 2025. Kerkez played the full match in the recent 4-0 win over Manchester United, but the wider view internally is said to centre on whether a higher ceiling is needed in that position. Lewis Hamilton also came to halt after his Ferrari lost power, with a virtual safety car deployed so the marshals could come to the seven-time world champion's aid. The McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri plus Red Bull's Max Verstappen completed the top five at the Lusail International Circuit, with the trio setting soft-tyre times that were more than four tenths adrift of the two Mercedes. The first red flag was to clear gravel off the track after an incident for Ferrari's Charles Leclerc early on, while the other was to recover the Alpine of Pierre Gasly following a high-speed spin. Frenchman Gasly hit a marker board before beaching himself after taking too much kerb at Turn 14 in the middle of the qualifying simulation runs. The interruptions led to the second hour being extended by 13 minutes to allow drivers more time on track in the representative conditions. Hamilton also had a moment with Verstappen that was noted by the race control. The Briton was on a flying lap when he got too close to the Dutchman, who was on a long run. Verstappen said Hamilton had moved under braking, but the stewards decided no further investigation was needed. The second Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was sixth on the timesheets, with Leclerc leading Hamilton in seventh and eighth, 1.3 seconds away from Antonelli's time. The two Racing Bulls of British rookie Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson were ninth and 10th. Leclerc had to head back into the garage after spinning and going through the gravel when Lawson was just ahead of him at Turn Nine. The Monegasque driver said the car did not feel right, and the Italian team spent a chunk of time repairing the damage to the floor. Antonelli, who secured his maiden title in Mexico City earlier this month, was also fastest in the opening session on the mediums. Mercedes did fit the 20-year-old with the soft tyre in the first hour, but he failed to set a lap time on them. Drivers will be limited to a maximum of 27 laps on a set of tyres at the Lusail International Circuit, meaning teams will have to make at least two pit stops during the 57-lap grand prix on Sunday, which starts at 16:00 GMT. The decision is caused by concern over the integrity of the Pirelli tyres on the high-speed, 16-corner track. Laps to the grid, formation laps and any laps completed after the end of the race will not be included. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
